disease_label_per_paper: Paraneoplastic chronic DIC from occult metastatic lung cancer followed by acute bleeding DIC and fatal intracranial hemorrhage
presentation_summary: 57-year-old man with prior DVT on rivaroxaban and recent Takotsubo cardiomyopathy presented with dyspnea, hemoptysis, syncope, hypoxemia, hypotension, and pulmonary embolism.
He had recurrent thrombosis despite anticoagulation, raising suspicion for an occult paraneoplastic process.
One month later he was readmitted with spontaneous dorsal hematoma, ecchymosis at venipuncture sites, hemoptysis, thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/INR, very high D-dimer, and hypofibrinogenemia.
During ICU deterioration he developed sudden altered consciousness; head CT showed right frontal hematoma with subarachnoid/subdural extension and herniation.
Autopsy identified metastatic lung cancer, supporting malignancy-associated chronic DIC that converted to acute DIC.

course_observations.description: Initial thoracic CT angiography confirmed a peripheral pulmonary embolism of the lower left lobe with bilateral pleural effusion and lower-lobe consolidation.
Readmission with spontaneous dorsal hematoma, ecchymosis on venipuncture sites, hemoptysis, platelets 93,000/ul, PT 26 seconds, INR 2.23, D-dimer >32.50 mg/L, and fibrinogen 162 mg/dL.
Sudden loss of consciousness with GCS 7; head CT showed right frontal hematoma with subarachnoid/subdural extension, cerebral compression, and herniation.
Despite mannitol, fibrinogen, fresh frozen plasma, and platelet pool, intracranial bleeding continued and the patient progressed to brain death.

quality_warnings: Autopsy lung cancer is confirmatory trigger evidence, not an ordinary observation.
Exact oxygen saturation and blood pressure were not reported; hypoxemia/hypotension are encoded with quality_note rather than quoted numeric values.
The case intentionally preserves both chronic thrombotic DIC evidence and later acute bleeding DIC evidence.
